result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give concrete, usable designs with search up front and thorough zero-result recovery. B handles the library's real tasks better: renew is one tap from Home, Home shows today's hours, the card barcode is always one tap away, and it adds barcode scan and Ask a librarian. A says more about what the app remembers, including scroll position, search text and filters that carry across screens. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers lay out usable screens with a prominent search field, detailed typing behavior and good recovery when a search finds nothing. B goes further on what the app remembers: it explains how the branch is chosen, keeps filters, search text and scroll position, and returns people to their task after sign-in. It also adds hold placement with undo and accessibility details. A is stronger on one-tap renew and access to the card barcode, but overall B covers the rubric a little more fully.
